CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
48-year-old female presents with shortness of breath that occurs with mild exercise or walking, such as up the driveway. She reports associated palpitations. She notes the shortness of breath has been happening more often lately. She is uncertain if it is related to her chronic back pain. She reports recently increasing her exercise to lose weight gained during COVID. Previously smoking two packs per day, she has reduced to approximately one cigarette per day.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies any other issues bothering her at this time.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Smoking history
Chronic back pain

MEDICATIONS
Effexor for depression
Gabapentin (Neurontin) for chronic back pain

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Tobacco: Currently smoking approximately one cigarette per day, reduced from two packs per day. Patient is making lifestyle changes as she gets older. Exercise: Recently increasing exercise to lose COVID-related weight gain. Has discussed doing yoga but has not made it a habit yet.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Physical exam appears normal other than mild wheezes heard in all lung fields.

RESULTS
Pulmonary function tests: Suggest possible asthma or COPD.
Chest X-ray: Flattened diaphragm noted, consistent with COPD often seen in smokers.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Patient is unable to exhale appropriately. Started on Combivent inhaler, two puffs twice daily. Albuterol inhaler prescribed for rescue use as needed when experiencing shortness of breath. Prednisone taper pack prescribed. Depression stable; continue Effexor. Continue Gabapentin (Neurontin) for chronic back pain management. Patient encouraged to do yoga for depression and back pain management.
